source.title: Investigating the Edge of Stability Phenomenon in Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: Rares Iordan; M. Deisenroth; Mihaela Rosca

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether edge-of-stability dynamics extend to off-policy deep reinforcement learning across data regimes and losses.
record.gate_note: The paper measures Hessian eigenvalues and loss behavior, not training classification error. It reports results in text for the plotted settings; cited supervised-learning findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests the edge-of-stability component of V5 in a new setting: off-policy reinforcement learning. It measures Hessian sharpness relative to the optimizer's stability threshold together with loss trajectories, including full-batch experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the main conclusion: edge-of-stability dynamics can occur in off-policy deep RL, with strong offline DQN results and weaker or inconsistent online and C51 results. It should also acknowledge Appendix A.3: offline C51 without momentum does show edge-of-stability behavior, so C51's failure is not universal and optimizer choice matters.
record.recipe_differences: Applies gradient descent with and without momentum to off-policy DQN and C51 in MinAtar reinforcement-learning settings; the cited claim concerns supervised-learning networks and squared-loss training.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed dynamics vary with algorithm/loss (DQN versus C51), data regime (offline versus online), and optimizer setting (momentum versus no momentum).
record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code and data will be made publicly available upon acceptance.
record.peer_reviewed: HLD 2023: 1st Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics
record.problems: Experiments are on the MinAtar environment and the authors call for testing more environments. They focus on loss behavior and do not establish a connection between Hessian eigenvalues and agent performance. Results are substantially described through figures; numerical uncertainty is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional plotted results for C51 and DQN across optimizer and environment settings in Appendix A (Figures 3, 6–13). These are not separately extracted here because the text gives overlapping aggregate descriptions, and the selected rows capture the main positive, absent, and condition-dependent outcomes.

untested.parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model-size effects, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

The catapult mechanism in wide squared-loss networks: initially supercritical learning-rate sweeps, transient loss growth followed by curvature reduction and low loss, divergence at larger rates, and divergence despite initially subcritical rates. The RL experiments do not directly replicate the fixed supervised objectives of the original studies.
Batch-normalization comparisons and normalization-free Fixup training.

missing.what: Add the full-batch DQN greedy-buffer result, separating its clear initial edge-of-stability phase from its later breakdown with increased instabilities. R8 records only C51, and rows_left_out does not identify Figures 4a–5.

record.verdict_notes: These verdicts concern V5's edge-of-stability component, not its catapult-recovery component. Additional appendix settings are declared in rows_left_out and therefore are not listed as missing. Those include the positive offline C51 results without momentum, offline DQN results on Space Invaders, and transient online edge-of-stability behavior on Space Invaders without momentum. Algorithm and loss change together between DQN and C51, so their comparison does not isolate loss as the cause.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width.
Depth, identity shortcuts, and training error in plain versus residual networks.
Initialization, signal propagation, and trainable depth.

Tests DQN and C51 on MinAtar rather than wide supervised-learning networks; it does not report training loss reaching a low value after a brief rise as a general recovery result. It studies mini-batch and full-batch gradient descent with and without momentum, not the cited full-batch supervised settings exclusively.
